entry.title: A New-Era of Learning for Support from SAP - Support Accreditation 2026 Release is here!
entry.content:
Support is evolving faster than ever. AI is transforming how we search for answers, resolve issues, collaborate with experts, and proactively maintain our SAP landscapes. As these experiences evolve, learning must evolve too.

That is why we are excited to introduce the completely reimagined Support Accreditation with the 2026 release, a modern learning journey designed to help SAP customers, partners, and employees maximize every interaction with support from SAP.

Whether you are new to SAP support or an experienced administrator, consultant, or IT professional, Support Accreditation equips you with the knowledge to work smarter, resolve issues faster, and unlock the full value of your SAP investment. All in about 60 minutes!

 

Why complete Support Accreditation?

Support Accreditation is so much more than an online course. It is your practical guide to navigating SAP's support ecosystem confidently, from preventing issues before they occur to leveraging AI-powered capabilities that simplify your daily work.

After completing the learning journey, you will know how to:

  • Maximize your SAP support experience using the right support channels at the right time
  • Resolve issues faster through intelligent self-service capabilities
  • Discover AI-powered innovations available in SAP for Me
  • Leverage SAP Cloud ALM and scenario-specific support offerings
  • Engage with support from SAP more effectively throughout your support journey
  • Earn an official digital Support Accreditation badge that recognizes your expertise

What’s new in 2026?

The 2026 release represents the largest transformation of Support Accreditation since its launch. Instead of simply updating existing lessons, we redesigned the entire learning journey around the way customers actually engage with support today.

A learning journey built around your support experience

The course now follows a natural end-to-end support journey, guiding learners from preventive support and self-service to case creation, expert engagement, autonomous resolution, and AI-assisted support. Throughout the journey, avatars will act as your guide, helping connect concepts into a realistic support experience while highlighting practical takeaways you can immediately apply in your daily work.

Built for the AI era

Aligned with SAP's AI  strategy, the new release introduces the latest intelligent support innovations, including Joule in SAP for Me, Intelligent Search, Incident Solution Matching, Support Assistant, Product Prediction Service, and Joule in SAP for Me, helping learners understand how AI is transforming the support experience.

 

More engaging, practical, and easier to learn

Lessons have been redesigned into shorter, focused modules that are easier to consume, with clear "When to use what" guidance to help you choose the right support tools and channels for every scenario. The learning journey now includes new walkthrough videos, updated screenshots, lesson summaries, and scenario-based quizzes that reinforce real-world decision-making and help you confidently apply your knowledge.

Start your learning journey today

Support is becoming more intelligent, more proactive, and increasingly AI-driven. The new Support Accreditation has been designed to help you stay ahead of these changes while building practical skills you can immediately apply in your daily work.

Complete the learning course, earn your digital Support Accreditation badge, and experience a new era of learning for support from SAP - https://learning.sap.com/courses/getting-started-with-support-from-sap-support-accreditation

entry.title: AI is Transforming Support: Navigating the Autonomous Enterprise
entry.content:
At SAP Sapphire 2026, SAP introduced its vision for the Autonomous Enterprise—a future where AI agents are embedded into business processes, helping organizations operate with greater speed, intelligence, and resilience. But what does this vision mean for Technical Support?

In the latest episode of the SAP Change Makers Podcast, Oliver Huschke speaks with Uwe Wieditz, VP and Global Head of Private Cloud ERP Technical Support, and Bernhard Luecke, Senior Director, Technical Support in Private Cloud ERP, about how AI is transforming SAP Support from a reactive problem-solving function into a proactive, predictive, and increasingly autonomous operation.

Their discussion explores how agentic AI, multi-agent orchestration, and human expertise are coming together to deliver faster resolutions, improved system stability, and a better customer experience.

 “The Autonomous Enterprise vision means AI agents are becoming operators embedded directly into enterprise processes. Thinking about this concept in the support context, it means we are shifting from reactive case handling to proactive, predictive, and increasingly autonomous support operations.”
— Uwe Wieditz

“The traditional case model is being redesigned. In the Autonomous Enterprise model, many cases will never need to be created at all: Step-by-step, AI agents detect, diagnose, and resolve issues autonomously. For cases that still need human involvement, AI simplifies the experience dramatically. Customers describe their problem in natural language; agents classify, prioritize, and route instantly. Engineers receive a pre-analyzed case with suggested resolutions — not a blank ticket."                 

— Bernhard Luecke

Key Takeaways

  •   Better outcomes for customers. AI-powered support helps increase system stability, resolve issues in minutes, and accelerate customers’ journey toward the Autonomous Enterprise.
  •   The evolution of the support engineer. Support engineers are moving from reactive problem solvers to AI agent orchestrators, focusing on complex challenges while bringing empathy and human connection to customer interactions.
  •   Trust comes first. Security, compliance, and responsible AI governance remain non-negotiable foundations of SAP’s AI-powered support strategy.

entry.title: Digitalisierung und Skalierung von Change Management: Erkenntnisse aus der SAP Kaffee-Ecke
entry.content:
Die monatliche SAP Change und Training Kaffee-Ecke widmete sich einem hochaktuellen Thema: Wie lassen sich Change Management-Prozesse in SAP-Projekten digitalisieren und skalieren? PD Dr. Oliver Kohnke, Global Service Owner for Organizational Change Management bei SAP, gab Einblicke in die Herausforderungen, Lösungsansätze und die neue AI-Assisted User Learning and Change Management App.

Warum wird Skalierung immer wichtiger?

Die Eingangsfrage an die Teilnehmenden machte deutlich: In den meisten Organisationen ist die Digitalisierung von Change Management bereits ein wichtiges Thema. Die Hälfte der Teilnehmenden stimmten dieser Aussage voll und ganz zu.

Die zweite Frage fokussierte sich auf die Herausforderungen, die bei der Digitalisierung von Change Management bestehen und gab zentrale Hinweise, die es in der Praxis zu berücksichtigen gilt: Akzeptanz steht mit deutlichem Abstand an erster Stelle, gefolgt von Kompetenz und Widerständen. Weitere genannte Aspekte waren fehlendes Verständnis, Budget- und Kapazitätsmangel, fehlende Plattformen sowie Ängste und Verunsicherung. Der Hinweis auf "Human in the Loop" verdeutlicht: Trotz KI-Unterstützung müssen Menschen im Prozess verbleiben.

Welche Herausforderungen bestehen bei der Digitalisierung von Change Management?

Die abschließende Frage ergab, dass die praktische Erfahrung mit Change Management-Apps in der Community noch begrenzt ist – die meisten Teilnehmenden haben bisher keine Berührungspunkte mit solchen Tools gesammelt.

Was treibt die Notwendigkeit zur Digitalisierung und Skalierung von Change Management? Oliver Kohnke stellte gleich zu Beginn klar: Der technologische Wandel vollzieht sich schneller als Mitarbeitende und Organisationen ihn adaptieren können. Die zentrale Herausforderung ist dabei nicht die Technologie selbst, sondern die Adoption – also die Annahme und Nutzung neuer Technologien. Gleichzeitig ist die kontinuierliche, manuelle Anpassung von Trainings- und Change Management-Inhalten zu langsam und die Kosten zu hoch. Um diese Herausforderungen zu bewältigen, müssen Change Management und Training ebenfalls schneller und effizienter werden.

Welche Vision verfolgt SAP?

SAP möchte Organizational Change Management Services und Tools anbieten, die “fully digitized, low touch, easy to use und highly scalable” sind. Diese Skalierbarkeit ist entscheidend, da SAP weltweit eine große Anzahl von Cloud-Implementierungen begleitet. Das Ziel: Kunden und Partner sollen die Angebote einfach und schnell nutzen können.

Um skalieren zu können, ist die Digitalisierung der standardisierten Methodik und Inhalte eine wesentliche Voraussetzung.

SAP nutzt seit Jahren eine “Best Practice” Change Management Methodologie. Der SAP Change Management-Ansatz ist auf SAP’s Activate Implementierungsmethodik abgestimmt und beinhaltet sechs Dimensionen: Change Strategy, Change Leadership, Change Communication, Change Realization, Change Enablement und Change Activeness.

 

Welche digitalen Assets stellt SAP bereit?

Methodik im SAP Activate Roadmap Viewer

Die Change Management Methodik ist über den SAP Activate Roadmap Viewer kostenfrei verfügbar. Diese Kundenplattform bietet Roadmaps für verschiedene SAP-Produkte auf Basis der globalen Implementierungsmethodik.

Der Change Management-Ansatz ist dort entsprechend der Activate-Phasen mit 18 Deliverables, 72 Tasks, 50 Tools & Templates und 10 Weblinks hinterlegt. Eine Registrierung auf sap.com ist notwendig, um die Tools und Templates nutzen zu können.

Ein besonderer Vorteil: Der Roadmap Viewer hat eine direkte Verbindung zu SAP Cloud Application Lifecycle Management (CALM). Wer CALM nutzt, kann die Deliverables und Templates direkt in das Tool laden und als Change Manager damit arbeiten.

SAP Learning Journeys und Zertifizierung

Um Kunden und Partnern die Nutzung der Change Managememt Methodik zu erleichtern, bietet SAP verschiedene Learning Courses an, die in einer Learning Journey unter dem Titel "Managing the People Side of SAP Cloud Projects" zusammengefasst sind. Die Lerninhalte werden auf Basis von verschiedenen Projektszenarien praxisnah vermittelt und sind über die Plattform learning.sap.com kostenfrei verfügbar.

Abschliessen kann man die Lernpfade mit einer offiziellen SAP Zertifizierung. Die Zertifizierung erfolgt AI unterstützt: In einem interaktiven Szenario mit einem Avatar werden Prüflinge in realitätsnahen Szenarien getestet . Die Zertifizierung ist entweder über ein Abonnement des SAP Learning Hub abrufbar oder kann im Trainingsshop der SAP erworben werden.

OCM in den SAP Success Plans

Das neue Service und Support Offering der SAP, die Success Plans, beinhaltet drei aufeinander aufbauende Layers: Foundational, Advanced und Max. Der Foundational und Advanced Success Plan beinhalten bereits verschiedene Change Management und Learning Services. Für den Max Success Plan sind die Inhalte zum Zeitpunkt der Coffee Corner Session noch in Arbeit).

Alle oben beschriebenen Angebote (SAP Activate Roadmap Viewer, CALM, Learning Journeys) sind auch Teil des Foundational Success Plan, den jeder Cloud Kunde automatisch erhält.

Mit dem Advanced Success Plan bekommen Kunden darüber hinaus Zugang zu verschiedenen standardisierten Change Management- und Learning-Services und Experten. Die Angebote stehen seit Mai 2026 zur Verfügung:

Darüber hinaus sind mehrere Change Management und Learning Advisory Services für den Max Success Plan in Arbeit.

 

Was leistet die neue AI-Assisted User Learning and Change Management App?

Im Juni 2026 ging die AI-Assisted User Learning and Change Management App in die General Availability. Die Anwendung ist über den SAP Micro-App Hub verfügbar. Fokus der ersten Version sind die Lernfunktionalitäten wie AI assisted Lernbedarfsanalyse und Lerninhalterstellung. Darüber hinaus bietet die App auch erste Funktionen zur Unterstützung von Change cManagement in Projekten zur Verfügung, auf die wir uns in dieser Session konzentriert haben.

Welche Funktionen bietet die App User Learning and Change Management?

Die erste Version konzentriert sich auf vier zentrale Change-Aktivitäten:

Stakeholder-Identifikation - Der Startpunkt jedes Change-Projekts:

Auf Basis von SAP Best Practices bietet die App vordefinierte Listen mit typischen betroffenen Rollen, die kundenspezifisch anpassbar sind. Wichtige Informationen wie Anzahl der betroffenen Personen, Line of Business und regionale Verteilung lassen sich für jede Stakeholdergruppe erfassen.

Die App unterstützt derzeit SAP Best Practices für S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition und Public Edition sowie einige SuccessFactors-Module. Die Integration weiterer SAP-Lösungen ist in Arbeit.

Change Story - Das Fundament der Change-Kommunikation:

Die App strukturiert diese nach Need for Change (Current Reality, Drivers, Alternatives), Future Vision, Implementation Approach (Key Facts and Figures), Value and Impact sowie Core Messaging. Alle Informationen, die typischerweise in Entscheidungsgremien vor Projektstart erstellt und diskutiert werden, lassen sich zentral dokumentieren. Das Ziel: Keine gemischten Botschaften, sondern konsistente Kommunikation. Die Change Story kann generell und für spezifische Stakeholdergruppen erstellt werden.

Kommunikationsanalyse:

Change Manager müssen wissen, welche Kanäle verfügbar sind – von Intranet-Portalen über Employee Meetings bis zu E-Mails oder Blogs. Die App hilft bei der Identifikation und Zuordnung geeigneter Kanäle für verschiedene Stakeholder-Gruppen. Auch Aspekte wie bidirektionale vs. unidirektionale Kommunikation, Frequenz und Kosten des Kanalbespielens können so leicht berücksichtigt werden. Darüber hinaus können auch für die identifizierten Stakeholdergruppen konkrete Kommunikationsbedarfe erfasst werden.

Kommunikationsplan - Das zentrale Arbeitstool für Change Manager:

Hier werden alle Kommunikationsmaßnahmen mit Zielgruppen, Kanälen, Timing und Status geplant und können auf einer Zeitschiene visualisiert werden. Durch eine farbliche Markierung der Kommunikationsmaßnahmen wird sofort ersichtlich, ob es sich um bidirektionale Kommunikation (wie Mitarbeitermeetings) oder unidirektionale Kommunikation (wie Projektankündigungen) handelt und letztlich ein guter Kommunikationsmix geplant wurde.

Ist die App auch für Nicht-SAP-Projekte nutzbar?

Eine wichtige Frage aus der Community: Kann die App auch für andere Change-Projekte genutzt werden, etwa die Einführung eines CRM- oder TMS-Systems? Die Antwort ist eindeutig Ja. Stakeholder-Identifikation, Change Story Kommunikationskanäle – und bedarfe sowie der Kommunikationsplan können für jedes beliebige Change-Projekt genutzt werden. Der besondere Benefit für SAP-Projekte liegt in der Verknüpfung zu den SAP Business Best Practices.

Welche KI-Features sind geplant?

Bis Ende 2026 will SAP entscheiden, wo KI im Change Management-Bereich den maximalen Mehrwert bringt. Das langfristige Ziel ist ambitioniert: personalisierte Massenkommunikation für SAP-Projekte. Bei vielen betroffenen Mitarbeitenden soll die KI rollenspezifische Botschaften generieren, die nah an deren Business-Realität sind.

Wie soll das funktionieren?

Kundenspezifische Projektdokumente – PowerPoint-Präsentationen, Entscheidungsmemos, Scope-Dokumente – sollen in die App hochgeladen werden können. Darüber hinaus sollen Schnittstellen zu Signavio und CALM SAP-spezifischen Inhalt bereitstellen. Die KI extrahiert daraus die relevanten Change-Elemente für die Change Story: Was ist im Scope, warum wird das Projekt gemacht, was ist die Urgency, welche Vision wird verfolgt? Change Manager können dann darauf aufbauen und die Story mit Key Stakeholdern reflektieren und anpassen.

Weitere geplante Features sind die Ergänzung um Stakeholder-Analyse und Change Impact-Analyse – beides Kernaktivitäten eines Change Managers – sowie die automatische Generierung von rollenbasierten Kommunikationsplänen und -inhalten.

Wie wird Qualität sichergestellt?

Ein kritischer Aspekt wurde diskutiert: Die Change Story ist das Fundament der gesamten Change-Kommunikation und entsteht idealerweise im Dialog. Ist eine Tool-basierte Erstellung nicht problematisch?

Oliver Kohnke betonte: "Der Output muss reviewed werden. Es bleibt jedem Change Manager freigestellt, die Change Story mit wichtigen Stakeholdern, dem Project Sponsor oder im Projektteam zu reflektieren und anzupassen." Das Konzept des **"Human in the Loop"** ist zentral – die KI beschleunigt, ersetzt aber nicht die fachliche Bewertung.

Wie ist die Mehrsprachigkeit geregelt?

Bei internationalen Projekten ist Kommunikation in lokalen Sprachen entscheidend. Ist Mehrsprachigkeit verfügbar? Das Tool selbst ist momentan nur in Englisch verfügbar – dem Servicemodell geschuldet, um globale Skalierbarkeit zu ermöglichen.

Was kostet die App?

Die App ist über den SAP Micro-App Hub verfügbar. Die Foundational Features (Basisfunktionalitäten ohne AI) kosten 1.140 Euro pro Jahr für 5 Nutzer.

Die Lizenzen richten sich an Change Manager und Learning Manager – nicht an Endanwendende.

Wie funktioniert das Pricing für KI-Features?

Für AI-gestützte Funktionen gilt ein verbrauchsbasiertes Modell mit 7 Euro pro AI Unit**. Jede durch die KI generierte Seite Learning Content wird als "Page" gezählt. Bei der Generierung von 10.000 Pages innerhalb eines Monats würde der Monatspreis bei etwa 8.050 Euro liegen.

Welche Effizienzgewinne wurden bereits erreicht?

Die entscheidende Frage: Gibt es bereits Erfahrungen zu Produktivitätsgewinnen? Die Antwort ist beeindruckend: Ergebnisse aus dem Early Adoption Programm zeigten Effizienzgewinne von 50 bis 60 Prozent bei der AI-basierten Durchführung von Lernbedarfsanalysen und Generierung von Learninginhalten.

Fazit: Change Management wird messbar effizienter

Die Digitalisierung und Skalierung von Change Management ist keine Zukunftsvision mehr, sondern bereits Realität. SAP zeigt mit der neuen App einen pragmatischen Weg auf, wie Change Manager durch Standardisierung, Digitalisierung und KI-Unterstützung erhebliche Zeitgewinne erzielen können.

Die bereits erreichten Effizienzgewinne im Learning-Bereich zeigen auch das Potenzial für den Change Management-Bereich. Gleichzeitig bleibt die Herausforderung bestehen, Akzeptanz für diese digitalen Werkzeuge zu schaffen – genau jener Punkt, der auch in der Eingangsumfrage als größtes Hindernis identifiziert wurde.

Die Kombination aus bewährter Methodik, strukturierten Tools und intelligenter Automatisierung verspricht, Change Management in SAP-Projekten auf ein neues Effizienzniveau zu heben – ohne die notwendige menschliche Expertise und den Dialog mit Stakeholdern zu ersetzen.

Die nächste Kaffee-Ecke nach der Sommerpause widmet sich KI-Tools und Use Cases in der täglichen Arbeit – mit interaktivem Austausch in Kleingruppen statt großer Vorträge.

entry.title: A close encounter with SAP Joule
entry.content:
Introduction

Here is a short recap of my close encounter with Joule to resolve a real-life question. The requirement was to print outbound delivery documents only after or during billing document posting. So the basic question was if outbound delivery output determination is triggered by billing document creation. I tried to settled that with AI. Here is how it worked for me.

Hi, Joule!

First, I tried to ask Joule on SAP support services portal.

Question:

Does billing document creation trigger output determination for relevant outbound deliveries

Response:

Creating a billing document does trigger output determination for the relevant outbound deliveries invoiced with that billing document. Output determination is generally processed at billing document creation, and this includes triggering outputs such as invoices or delivery notifications related to the outbound delivery being billed.

However, some specific scenarios, for example with return to vendor deliveries, may require additional correction notes or adjustments, but the standard process supports triggering output determination upon billing document creation for outbound deliveries.

Additionally, Joule gives a couple of links to support notes, that are not really relevant to the topic.

Hi, Gemini!

Then I asked Google Gemini.

Question:

Does billing document creation trigger output determination for relevant outbound deliveries in SAP

Response:

No, creating a billing document does not automatically trigger standard output determination for preceding outbound deliveries in SAP.

By default, the creation and saving of a billing document (such as an invoice) only evaluates and triggers output determination for the billing document itself (Application V3). It does not backtrack to re-evaluate or re-trigger standard output types belonging to the outbound delivery (Application V2).

However, because specific business processes require deliveries to react when they are fully invoiced, SAP provides technical and customized ways to achieve this.

Gemini provides links to multiple source materials including Q&A SAP Community pages, notably Trigger output determination on delivery, after billing is complete. 

At this point I was pretty sure Gemini is right, because when @Jelena_Perfiljeva says something, she is typically spot on. Nevertheless, being presented with two contradicting responses, I did some testing on my own. It confirmed the Gemini answer - outbound delivery output determination is not triggered by billing document posting.

Conclusion

My little experience is by no means any thorough comparison of Joule vs Gemini. My expectation though was that Joule would give a much better answer as it could access SAP internal, restricted sources like Knowledge Based Articles, support notes, internal documentation on top of public domain ones. To my surprise it looks like Joule was not trained on public domain pages, even if they are hosted by SAP. Joule missed references to the vast pool of knowledge on SAP community pages. In my opinion Joule would much better off, if it stood on two legs - on SAP proprietary and public domain knowledge.

entry.title: Designing a Knowledge Base Article Search Agent Using SAP AI Solutions
entry.content:
Enterprise Document Discovery Powered by SAP Business AI, SAP AI Core, SAP HANA Cloud Vector Engine, and SAP BTP

Executive Summary

The Business Problem

Enterprise knowledge is rarely centralised. Across most SAP customer organisations, critical information is distributed across Microsoft SharePoint sites, Microsoft 365 repositories, shared network folders, PDF documents, Word files, Excel workbooks, PowerPoint decks, and internal knowledge bases. Subject matter experts hold process knowledge in personal drives. Project teams maintain functional design documents and technical specifications in disconnected locations. Support teams manage Knowledge Base Articles (KBAs) in systems that are not easily searchable across the broader organisation.

The consequence is predictable, users cannot find the right document at the right time. They raise support tickets for issues that have already been resolved. They duplicate effort because existing process documentation is not discoverable. They depend on colleagues ‘tribal knowledge’ rather than structured, reusable content.

Traditional keyword search compounds the problem. Keyword-based retrieval matches exact terms, not intent. A user searching for "payment run error" will not retrieve a document titled "FI period-end processing failure" even if the content is directly relevant. Keyword search does not understand synonyms, contextual meaning, or the relationship between a user's question and the substance of a document. It returns results based on word frequency, not relevance.

The Proposed Solution

This whitepaper proposes how customers and service providers can architect and build a Knowledge Base Article (KBA) Search Agent built on top of SAP AI solutions. The agent enables users to submit natural language queries and receive ranked, relevant documents drawn from across the enterprise content landscape, regardless of where those documents are stored or what format they are in.

The agent is not a reporting tool or an analytics dashboard. Its purpose is knowledge discovery: helping users find the most relevant document for their query, faster and with greater confidence.

The business value is direct:

  • Faster issue resolution: Users find relevant KBAs, process guides, and technical specifications without manual searching across multiple repositories.
  • Improved knowledge reuse: Existing documentation is surfaced and consumed rather than recreated.
  • Reduced dependency on tribal knowledge: Institutional knowledge becomes discoverable and accessible to all authorised users.
  • Better user productivity: Time spent searching is reduced; time spent resolving issues or completing tasks is increased.

SAP Joule, SAP's generative AI digital assistant, already demonstrates this model within SAP's own product portfolio, allowing employees to ask questions in plain language and receive answers grounded in business data. The KBA Search Agent extends this principle to enterprise document repositories.

Reference Architecture

Architecture Overview

The KBA Search Agent is built on a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture. RAG combines the retrieval of relevant documents from a vector store with the contextual understanding of a large language model (LLM), enabling the agent to return results that are grounded in actual enterprise content rather than generated from model memory alone.

The architecture operates as follows: a user submits a natural language query through the interaction layer. The query is converted into a vector embedding using an embedding model accessed via the SAP Generative AI Hub. That embedding is used to perform a similarity search against the SAP HANA Cloud Vector Engine, which stores pre-computed embeddings of all indexed enterprise documents. The most semantically similar document chunks are retrieved, ranked, and returned to the user with source references and relevance indicators.

 

 

Key Components

User Interaction Layer Users interact with the agent through SAP Joule or a custom interface built using SAP Build. SAP Joule supports natural language queries and runs within SAP BTP environments, requiring authentication between SAP Cloud Identity, SAP BTP, and the target system. SAP Build enables low-code construction of a dedicated search interface where users can submit queries, view ranked results, and navigate to source documents.

 

Agent Orchestration Layer SAP AI Core serves as the runtime for the agent's orchestration logic. It manages the embedding model, the retrieval pipeline, and the connection to the SAP HANA Cloud Vector Engine. The SAP Generative AI Hub, available within SAP AI Core, provides access to foundation models and LLMs for both embedding generation and, where appropriate, response synthesis. SAP AI Launchpad provides the management and monitoring interface for AI models, deployments, and prompt configurations.

 

Enterprise Content Connectors SAP Integration Suite provides the integration layer for connecting to external content repositories including Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft 365, shared folders, and other enterprise document sources. Connectors extract document content and metadata. This includes file type, author, last modified date, source system, and access permissions for ingestion into the pipeline.

Document Ingestion and Chunking Pipeline Ingested documents are pre-processed to extract clean text from PDFs, Word documents, Excel files, and PowerPoint decks. Documents are then split into semantically coherent chunks, typically 300 to 500 tokens, to ensure that embedding vectors represent focused, retrievable units of content rather than entire documents. Metadata is extracted and associated with each chunk, including document title, source system, last modified date, document type, and access control attributes.

Embedding Model and Vector Store Each document chunk is passed to an embedding model via the SAP Generative AI Hub. The embedding model converts the text into a high-dimensional vector that captures its semantic meaning. These vectors are stored in the SAP HANA Cloud Vector Engine.

SAP HANA Cloud's Vector Engine supports vector CRUD operations through SQL and is purpose-built for use cases including semantic search, RAG, similarity search, recommendations, and classification. A key benefit is that vector data, relational data, metadata, and access control information can all reside within the same governed platform, simplifying data architecture and security management.

Semantic Search and Relevance Ranking Layer When a user submits a query, it is converted to an embedding using the same model used during ingestion. The SAP HANA Cloud Vector Engine performs a similarity search - using cosine similarity or L2 distance - to identify the document chunks most semantically proximate to the query vector. Results are then ranked using a composite relevance score that incorporates multiple signals (described in the Implementation section below).

Security and Access Control Layer Document-level permissions from source systems are preserved throughout the pipeline. Each document chunk is tagged with its source system access control metadata. At query time, the agent filters results to return only documents the requesting user is authorised to access. SAP BTP's role-based access control and SAP Cloud Identity services provide the authentication and authorisation framework.

 Implementation Approach

Phased Development Plan

A phased approach reduces delivery risk, allows early value realisation, and enables iterative refinement of relevance quality before broad rollout.

Phase 1 – Foundation

Step 1: Identify and Prioritise Document Sources

Begin by cataloguing the enterprise content landscape. Identify which repositories contain the highest-value knowledge for the target user group. For most SAP customers, the recommended starting point is SAP support KBAs, functional design documents (FDDs), technical specifications, and process documentation. Prioritise sources where users currently experience the greatest difficulty finding relevant content.

Step 2: Define KBA Taxonomy and Metadata Standards

Establish a consistent metadata schema across all document sources. Key metadata fields should include: document type, functional area, SAP module or product, author, creation date, last modified date, source system, access classification, and version. Consistent metadata is essential for effective filtering, ranking, and governance.

Step 3: Connect to Content Repositories

Use SAP Integration Suite to establish connectors to Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft 365, shared network folders, and other identified repositories. Configure authentication, access permissions, and incremental synchronisation schedules to ensure the index remains current as documents are created or updated.

Phase 2 – Ingestion and Indexing (offline)

 Step 4: Ingest, Preprocess, and Chunk Documents

Extract text from all supported document formats - PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and plain text. Apply preprocessing to remove headers, footers, and formatting artefacts. Split documents into chunks of approximately 300–500 tokens using a recursive character text splitter or equivalent approach, with a small overlap between adjacent chunks to preserve contextual continuity.

Step 5: Generate Embeddings and Store Vectors

Pass each chunk to the embedding model via the SAP Generative AI Hub. Store the resulting vectors in SAP HANA Cloud's Vector Engine alongside the associated metadata and chunk text. The SAP Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP) can serve as the application layer managing this pipeline, with native support for vector data types and integration with the SAP HANA Cloud ecosystem.

Step 6: Apply Metadata Enrichment and Document-Level Permissions

Enrich each stored chunk with its full metadata record. Associate source-system access control attributes with each chunk so that permission filtering can be applied at query time. Validate that permission inheritance from source systems (e.g., SharePoint site permissions) is correctly reflected in the index.

Phase 3 – Search, Ranking, and Pilot (online)

 Step 7: Implement Semantic Search and Relevance Scoring

Deploy the query pipeline: user query → embedding generation → vector similarity search → result retrieval. Implement a composite relevance ranking engine that combines multiple signals to produce a final ranked list of documents for each query.

Step 8: Relevance Ranking Signals

The ranking engine should incorporate the following signals:

Signal

Description

Semantic similarity

Cosine similarity score between query vector and document chunk vector

Document freshness

Recency of last modification date; more recently updated documents score higher

Source trust level

Configurable weighting by source type (e.g., official SAP KBA > internal wiki > email attachment)

Metadata match

Alignment between query context and document metadata (e.g., SAP module, document type)

Usage signals

Historical click-through and positive feedback data from prior user interactions

User context

User's role, functional area, or system context to personalise result relevance

Step 9: Test with Representative Queries and Pilot Users

Assemble a set of representative queries drawn from real user scenarios - support tickets, process questions, configuration queries. Evaluate retrieval quality by assessing whether the top-ranked results are genuinely relevant to each query. Engage a pilot user group of 10–20 users from the target functional area. Collect structured feedback on result relevance and usability. Iterate on chunking strategy, metadata weighting, and ranking logic based on findings before broader rollout.

Recommendations

Practical Guidance for SAP Customers

  1. Establish Data Readiness Before Indexing The quality of search results is directly dependent on the quality of the underlying content. Before indexing, assess document quality across target repositories. Remove outdated, duplicate, or superseded documents. Establish a content governance process to maintain index quality over time. Poorly governed content will produce poor search results regardless of the sophistication of the AI model.
  2. Start with a High-Value, Bounded Domain Do not attempt to index all enterprise content in the first phase. Begin with a single, high-value domain where the need for better knowledge discovery is clearly felt and measurable. Recommended starting points include:
  • SAP support KBAs and incident resolution guides
  • Functional design documents and technical specifications
  • SAP implementation project knowledge repositories
  • Process documentation for a specific SAP module (e.g., Finance, Procurement, HR)

A bounded scope enables faster delivery, clearer success measurement, and a more controlled environment for relevance tuning.

  1. Preserve and Enforce Source-Level Permissions Access control is non-negotiable. The agent must not surface documents to users who are not authorised to access them in the source system. Implement permission filtering at the retrieval layer, not as a post-processing step. Leverage SAP BTP's role-based access control and SAP Cloud Identity services to manage authentication. Regularly audit permission mappings as source system access controls change. SAP Joule is designed to be compliant with SAP product standards, AI ethics, and GDPR, providing a responsible AI foundation for the solution.
  2. Define Success Measures Before Rollout Establish clear, measurable success criteria prior to pilot launch. Recommended metrics include:
  • Retrieval precision: Percentage of top-5 results rated as relevant by users
  • Time-to-document: Reduction in average time taken to locate a relevant document
  • Support ticket deflection: Reduction in tickets raised for issues covered by indexed KBAs
  • User adoption rate: Percentage of target users actively using the agent within 60 days of launch
  1. Plan for Continuous Relevance Tuning Relevance quality degrades over time if the index is not maintained. Establish operational processes for: incremental document ingestion as new content is created; periodic re-indexing of modified documents; review and adjustment of ranking weights based on usage signal data; and regular user feedback collection. The SAP AI Launchpad provides monitoring and management capabilities to support ongoing model and pipeline oversight.

6. Adopt a Responsible AI Posture RAG architectures reduce the risk of LLM hallucination by grounding responses in retrieved documents rather than model-generated content. However, the agent should always surface source references alongside results, enabling users to verify the origin and authority of retrieved content. Implement confidence thresholds: if retrieved content is not sufficiently relevant to a query, the agent should indicate this rather than returning low-quality results.

7. Key Architectural Components The solution follows a two-core action model: an offline ingestion and indexing pipeline that processes, chunks, embeds, and stores enterprise documents; and an online query and retrieval pipeline that converts user queries to vectors, performs similarity search, applies access control filtering, and returns ranked results.

Layer

Component

Technology

User Interaction

Conversational search interface

SAP Joule / SAP Build Apps

Agent Orchestration

Application and domain logic, RAG pipeline coordination

SAP Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP)

AI Development

Pro-code agent construction, type-safe LLM integration

SAP Cloud SDK for AI

AI Services

Embedding model access, LLM access, prompt management, orchestration

SAP Generative AI Hub (via SAP AI Core)

AI Management

Model lifecycle, deployment monitoring, configuration

SAP AI Launchpad

Vector Store

Vector CRUD operations, cosine similarity / L2 distance search, metadata storage

SAP HANA Cloud Vector Engine

Knowledge Graph

Semantic relationship modelling, ontology-based reasoning, business context enrichment

SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine

Content Connectors

Integration to SharePoint, Microsoft 365, shared folders, document repositories

SAP Integration Suite

Document Ingestion

Text extraction from PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX; chunking; metadata extraction

CAP pipeline / SAP BTP Object Store

Security & Access Control

Role-based access control, authentication, source-level permission filtering

SAP BTP Authorization & Trust Management / SAP Cloud Identity

Connectivity

Secure on-premise and cloud system connectivity

SAP Connectivity Service / SAP Destination Service

Runtime

Application hosting

SAP BTP Cloud Foundry or Kyma runtime

Other Key Architectural Considerations

Security and Access Control

  • Document-level permissions from source systems (e.g., SharePoint site permissions) must be captured during ingestion and enforced at retrieval time — not as a post-processing step.
  • SAP BTP Authorization & Trust Management and SAP Cloud Identity Services provide the authentication and authorisation framework across all layers.
  • The SAP Generative AI Hub's built-in orchestration capabilities include data masking and I/O filtering, supporting responsible AI and GDPR compliance requirements.

Semantic Search Quality

  • SAP HANA Cloud's Vector Engine natively supports semantic search, RAG, similarity search, recommendations, classifications, and anomaly detection — all within a single multi-model database, simplifying data architecture and security management.
  • Combining vector data with relational metadata, graph relationships, and spatial data within a single platform enables richer, more context-aware retrieval.
  • RAG architectures ground LLM responses in retrieved enterprise content, reducing hallucination risk. Where retrieved content is insufficiently relevant, the agent should withhold a response rather than return low-quality results.

Scalability and Performance

  • The architecture is runtime-agnostic, supporting both SAP BTP Cloud Foundry and Kyma environments.
  • SAP HANA Cloud's in-memory architecture enables real-time similarity search at enterprise scale.
  • Incremental ingestion pipelines ensure the vector index remains current as documents are created, modified, or deleted in source systems.

Content Governance and Data Readiness

  • Index quality is directly dependent on content quality. Outdated, duplicate, or superseded documents should be removed before indexing and governed continuously thereafter.
  • A consistent metadata taxonomy (document type, functional area, SAP module, access classification, version) must be defined and enforced across all source repositories before ingestion begins.
  • Starting with a bounded, high-value domain — such as SAP support KBAs, functional design documents, or process documentation for a specific SAP module — reduces delivery risk and enables measurable relevance validation before broader rollout.

Responsible AI and Observability

  • SAP AI Launchpad provides centralised monitoring of model deployments, latency metrics, and usage patterns, supporting ongoing operational oversight.
  • All results must surface source references, enabling users to verify the origin and authority of retrieved content.
  • Confidence thresholds should be implemented: if no retrieved chunk meets a minimum similarity score, the agent should indicate that no sufficiently relevant document was found rather than returning misleading results.

Conclusion

The objective of the KBA Search Agent is not to generate analytics, produce dashboards, or report on document usage. Its purpose is singular and practical: to help users find the most relevant document for their query, across all available enterprise content sources, in the least amount of time.

SAP AI solutions - including SAP AI Core, the SAP Generative AI Hub, SAP HANA Cloud's Vector Engine, SAP Joule, SAP Build, SAP BTP, and SAP Integration Suite - provide a technically credible, enterprise-grade foundation for this capability. The combination of semantic search, vector embeddings, RAG, and composite relevance ranking addresses the fundamental limitations of keyword-based retrieval and delivers a qualitatively different knowledge discovery experience.

For SAP customers, this is not a speculative future capability. The underlying components are available today. The path to value is a phased, governed implementation that starts with a high-value content domain, establishes strong data and permission foundations, and iterates toward broader coverage based on demonstrated user value.

Enterprise knowledge exists. The challenge is making it findable. The KBA Search Agent, built on SAP AI solutions, is a practical and scalable answer to that challenge.

 

This whitepaper reflects SAP solution capabilities as of July 2026. Architects should validate specific feature availability prior to implementation.

entry.title: Step-by-Step Guide to Searching or Viewing Support Cases in SAP for Me
entry.content:
Are you having trouble viewing or managing your support cases in SAP for Me? This SAP Blog post is for you! 

 

 

 

Managing support cases shouldn’t feel like a maze. If you’re an SAP customer or partner, SAP for Me is your central hub — a one-stop portal where you can track, manage, and customize your support cases with ease. 

 

Here's a step-by-step guide on how to view or search for your support cases in SAP for Me.  

  1.  Login to SAP for Me using your S-user ID and password.  
  2. Under “Dashboards”, click on “Services & Support”.  
  3. Click on the “Cases” tab, to view your case list.

 

 

 

 

 

 

With the newly designed Case List, you will see two views: Default view and Personal view. 

Under Default view, you will see several case selection options: 

  • Open Cases - created by someone in your organization and that, based on your authorizations, you have access to view 
  • Closed Cases - were resolved and confirmed 
  • Drafts - have not been sent to SAP yet 
  • Favorites - case(s) marked as Favorite 
  • Auto Confirm - case(s) that will auto confirm soon 

You can sort and group the list, choose which type of cases shall be displayed, and narrow down the items to those most relevant to you by using a variety of filter criteria. This configuration can then be saved for future re-use, allowing you to switch between different views with ease.   

 

You may refer to this article Customizing the Case List help topic or refer to the Knowledge Base article (KBA) 2931236 for guidance on managing and customizing your case list. 

 

Additionally, using the central search box, you can filter or search for the specific case number as per the Knowledge Base article (KBA) 3363874 - How to search for a specific case number - SAP for Me. 

 

For more information, please refer to the Knowledge Base article (KBA) 1812813- How to view or search for cases - SAP for Me. 

 

________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Authorization Requirements: 

 Ensure your S-user ID must have the appropriate authorizations to manage and view support cases in SAP for Me. See Knowledge Base article (KBA) 3383142 - Which S-user ID authorizations are required for support case handling? 

To request the necessary authorizations, use the self-service process described in the Knowledge Base article (KBA) 2891528 or, contact your super administrator directly. See the super administrators in the company here: Users & Contacts - SAP for Me . 

________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Good News!  Meet Joule: Your AI Assistant

 

Did you know you can now search and view your support cases effortlessly using our newly integrated AI-powered driven “Joule” in SAP for Me?  

Yes, you read that right! SAP for Me now features Joule, an AI-powered assistant that transforms how you manage your cases. Instead of hunting for specific pages, you can simply type your intent, and Joule will direct you to the right dashboard in SAP for Me.  

 

Here’s how it works:  

1. Click the diamond icon (Joule) in the upper right corner of your screen, next to the notification bell, or use the banner to start typing your query.

 

 

2. Joule will analyze your request and display the specific case record. 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Note:  In addition to the cases you reported, Joule can also search and display support cases submitted by your colleagues or your SAP Partner under your company’s account.  

3. Click the case number to manage and open the case details. 

 

For more information and to better understand Joule in SAP for Me — its features, scope, and capabilities — you may refer to Knowledge Base article (KBA) 3740053 - Joule in SAP for Me - Scope and FAQ.  

 

You can also visit the SAP News Center https://news.sap.com/2026/06/sap-launches-joule-in-sap-for-me/ to learn more and subscribe to the newsletter for updates.  

 

And that’s it! Viewing and searching for cases in SAP for Me is straightforward once you know where to look. Whether you’re tracking an ongoing issue or reviewing a resolved case for reference, the Cases feature in SAP for Me puts all the information you need right at your fingertips. 

 

 

Got More Questions? 

 Please note that the Customer Interaction Center is always happy to guide you on any of the mentioned processes and assist you with any queries you may have!    
 

If you have any questions, please feel free to ask us in the Q&A  All Questions in Customer Experience | SAP Community and All Questions in Support Services | SAP Community  

 

Don't Miss Out on Free Webcasts  

 

 

 

 

We would like to invite you to our free webcasts, which we believe can help you get the best from your support in SAP. You can find all upcoming CIC Webcasts. These sessions are open to all the users and will revolve around hot topics in support today such as SAP for Me, Case Management, etc.  

Additionally, you can explore a range of CIC how-to videos at learning.sap.com. Please feel free to share this information with your colleagues. We are looking forward to your attendance.  

 

Lastly, you may want to access all CIC Blogs here:  https://community.sap.com/t5/tag/CustomerInteractionCenter/tg-p/board-id/crm-blog-sap.  

Thanks for reading!  We hope you found this guide helpful.

entry.title: Enhancing Your SAP Support Experience: How to Contact the Customer Interaction Center (CIC)
entry.content:
In today's fast-paced business environment, having reliable and efficient support for your SAP solutions is crucial. The Customer Interaction Center (CIC) is your go-to resource for a wide range of support needs, available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. Whether you need assistance with case management, user management, or navigating SAP for Me, the CIC team is here to help. In this blog, we'll guide you through the various ways you can contact CIC, including the webform/contact form option. 

 

 

 Product-Related Assistance

entry.title: Data Driven Change Management: What Two SAP S/4HANA Programmes Prove About Measuring Adoption
entry.content:
By Anthea Arnol, Change Consultant, Customer Engagement and Adoption ANZ, SAP.

Most organizations running SAP transformations invest in communication, training, and stakeholder engagement. The question that rarely gets answered with evidence is: is it actually working? What are the success factors?

Two Australian state government agencies, one in Queensland and one in New South Wales, tackled this question by deploying structured pulse check surveys before and after their OCM interventions. They measured, intervened, and measured again. The results don't just validate the approach. They show precisely what moves the needle on adoption readiness in SAP cloud programmes, and what doesn't.

This post summarizes the outcomes, identifies the interventions that drove measurable improvement, and offers practical recommendations for SAP project managers, IT leaders, and OCM practitioners running similar programmes.

Why Measuring Change Readiness Matters

Organizational Change Management has a credibility challenge. In many programmes, OCM activities are planned and executed:

  • Newsletters sent
  • Town halls held
  • Training sessions scheduled

Yet the question "did it work?" is often answered with anecdotes rather than data.

Pulse check surveys change that equation. A pulse check is a structured questionnaire deployed at key project milestones to measure:

  • Awareness
  • Understanding
  • Confidence
  • Sentiment

The first round establishes a baseline. The second round, deployed after targeted interventions, tells you whether your change approach is landing and where it isn't.

This shifts OCM from activity reporting ("we sent 14 newsletters and held 6 roadshows") to outcome reporting ("staff understanding increased by 43 points and negative sentiment dropped from 21% to 3%"). For sponsors and steering committees, that's the difference between faith and evidence.

Two Programmes with different Contexts

 

 

Queensland State Government

New South Wales State Government

🏛️ Agency

Agency 1

Agency 2

🚀Program

ECC6 → S/4HANA Public Cloud

ECC → S/4HANA Private Cloud

👥Audience

📋Survey Tool

💬Question Types

Multiple choice + free text

Multiple choice + free text

Different cloud deployment models, different team structures, and different levels of OCM resourcing. Yet the same OCM disciplines produced measurable results in both environments. That replicability is one of the most useful findings in the data.

What the Surveys Measured and What Improved

Both programmes measured comparable dimensions:

  • Project awareness
  • Understanding of impact
  • Information access
  • Communication effectiveness
  • Manager support
  • Change readiness
  • Confidence

Both showed improvements across all measured dimensions between Survey 1 and Survey 2.

 

The largest gains came from sentiment. People shifted from uncertainty to confidence. The drivers were:

  • Team-level "What This Means For You" communications
  • Myth-busting fact sheets that replaced speculation with verified information

Communication negative responses dropped from 21% at Survey 1 to just 3% at Survey 2. That shift came from:

  • A structured fortnightly email cadence
  • Change Champion reinforcement across the Finance Directorate

 

NSW started from a lower baseline and achieved the most dramatic improvements. The single largest gain, 57 points in manager support, came from equipping managers with:

  • A one-pager covering key messages
  • FAQs
  • Escalation paths

Information access moved from 13% to 63% after the team created:

  • One centralised SharePoint page
  • Clear headings
  • A bookmarkable link
  • Consistent embedding of the URL in project communications

People can't engage with a project they can't find.

The Interventions That Drove Real Results

Looking across both programmes, six categories of intervention consistently drove measurable improvements.

1. Manager Enablement (Highest Impact)

The approach was consistent:

  • Talking points
  • FAQs
  • Structured manager briefings
  • Team-specific impact information

NSW's +57 point uplift in manager support was the largest single-dimension gain across either programme. Queensland achieved 88% senior leader support at Survey 2 through visible executive endorsement and consistent leadership messaging.

The insight: managers are the highest-leverage channel in any SAP transformation.

2. Single Source of Truth

NSW improved information access by creating a dedicated SharePoint page featuring:

  • What's Changing
  • FAQs
  • Key Dates

Queensland similarly centralised project resources on SharePoint with visible "last updated" indicators and cross-stream links.

The principle: remove information friction before launching engagement activities.

3. Structured Communication Cadence

Both agencies established predictable communication rhythms:

  • Fortnightly project update emails
  • Monthly change newsletters
  • Scheduled management briefings

The key isn't communication volume. It's consistency.

4. Change Champion Networks

Both programmes activated change champion networks to:

  • Cascade messages
  • Create trusted team-level touchpoints
  • Extend communication reach
  • Reinforce key messages locally

Queensland refreshed its Champion forum with structured agendas including:

  • Report Back segments
  • Key messages to cascade
  • Business Readiness updates

5. Concrete Benefits Messaging

NSW's confidence in project success grew from 23% to 58% after the team introduced:

  • Before-and-after process examples
  • Practical demonstrations of future-state ways of working

Abstract statements don't convert uncertain people. Concrete examples do.

6. Feedback Loops

Both agencies implemented:

  • "You Asked / We Did" mechanisms
  • Visible responses to staff concerns
  • Ongoing feedback channels

Closing the feedback loop reduces reliance on rumour and informal networks while building trust in the formal change programme.

Practical Recommendations for SAP Change Programmes

  • Start with measurement. Deploy a baseline pulse check early in your programme. Without it, you're guessing where to invest your OCM effort.
  • Equip managers before anything else - e.g. a one-pager with talking points, 5-6 FAQs, Guidance on where to direct questions can be more effective than any all-staff email campaign.
  • Build information infrastructure first: Create a single, findable, up-to-date source of truth before launching engagement campaigns. Embed the link everywhere.
  • Commit to a communication cadence and maintain it: Fortnightly or monthly, pick a rhythm and don't break it. Consistency matters more than frequency.
  • Show, don't tell: Replace abstract benefit statements with concrete process comparisons.
  • Close the loop visibly: Respond publicly to concerns and demonstrate what changed as a result.
  • Measure again: Deploy Survey 2 after interventions have had time to land. Compare. Report. Adjust.

What This Means for Data-Driven OCM: These two programmes demonstrate that structured OCM practice is both replicable and measurable.

Across different Organisational contexts, Project scopes, Cloud deployment models, OCM resourcing levels, the same disciplines consistently improved readiness:

  • Manager enablement
  • Communication cadence
  • Single source of truth
  • Feedback loops
  • Benefits messaging

The intensity of support matters less than the consistency and structure of the interventions applied.
