entry.title: Why SAP support tickets keep coming back, and how to break the cycle
entry.content:
Every SAP support team knows the ticket that gets closed on Monday and reopens the following month, slightly reworded. The fix worked, the user was unblocked, and yet the problem came back. If your ticket count never seems to go down no matter how busy the team is, this post is for you.

Rather than explain problem management in the abstract, I want to walk through one case from an application support engagement I led, because it shows exactly why this happens and what actually stops it. Here is what follows: the ticket pattern as it showed up in the queue, what the root cause turned out to be in SAP configuration and master data, the fix, the numbers before and after, and the general method I now use on every support engagement. The customer was a mid-sized manufacturing company running SAP ECC 6.0, and the ticket that kept coming back lived in Materials Management.

The pattern: sixteen tickets that were really one problem

We started by pulling 90 days of ticket history from the service desk: 220 tickets. Reading through them, a set of MM tickets stood out that looked unrelated on the surface:

  • "Release strategy not triggered on purchase order" (raised from ME21N, escalated because ME29N showed nothing to release)
  • "Purchasing spend report shows a blank category for several materials" (ME2M and the monthly spend report, both grouped by material group)
  • "Condition record not found when creating a PO for material ..." (price not determined at item level)
  • "Purchase requisition cannot be converted to a PO" (ME57 / ME21N)

Sixteen tickets in 90 days, from four requesters across two plants. Each one was closed within a day or two. The fix, every time, was the same: the consultant opened MM02, maintained the material group on the Basic Data 1 view, and asked the user to retry. It worked every time. The SLA was met every time. And every few days another one arrived, with different wording, from a different user.

What the root cause looked like in SAP terms

The turning point was clustering the tickets by the object they referenced, not by how they were worded. All sixteen pointed at materials with an empty material group (MARA-MATKL), and every one of those materials was a finished good (material type FERT).

The next question was why finished goods were being created with a blank group. There were two paths, and both were allowed by the system:

  1. Field selection. For the field reference assigned to material type FERT (OMS2), the material group field was set to optional in the field selection (OMS9). So MM01 accepted a blank group without complaint.
  2. Inbound interface. Most new finished goods did not come from MM01 at all. They arrived from the product lifecycle system as MATMAS IDocs, and the mapping never populated the material group. Because the field was optional, the IDocs posted cleanly with status 53. Nobody saw a failure, because there was none to see.

Then, why did a blank group break so many different things? Because three downstream processes depended on it without anyone having written that dependency down:

  • The PO release strategy used material group as a characteristic (CEKKO-MATKL). With no group, no strategy was determined, so the PO either went through unreleased or stalled, depending on the value.
  • The purchasing pricing access sequence had a step keyed on material group, so price determination failed at item level.
  • The spend reporting aggregated by material group, so the spend on those materials landed in a blank bucket.

This is the distinction that matters. The trigger was "someone created a material without a group." The cause was "the system allowed it, and three processes silently depended on it." Sixteen incidents, one problem.

One more check made the size of the problem clear. A query on MARA for FERT materials with a blank MATKL returned over 200 materials, not just the eight that had already generated tickets. The ticket queue was showing us the leading edge of a much larger backlog. Every one of those materials was a future ticket waiting for its first PO.

The permanent fix, which was mostly not code

  1. Configuration. Material group set to required for the FERT field reference in OMS9, transported through the normal landscape. One entry, half a day including testing in QA.
  2. Interface. The MATMAS mapping was corrected to derive the material group from the product hierarchy the lifecycle system already sends. Where derivation fails, the IDoc now stops in error (status 51) instead of posting an incomplete material. A visible failure in WE02 replaced a silent gap.
  3. Data. A one-time mass correction with MM17 on MARA-MATKL for the 200-plus existing materials, values derived from the product hierarchy and signed off by the MM lead before the run.
  4. Ownership. A weekly check for blank material groups by material type, owned by the master data team rather than the support desk. If it ever shows a row, that is a defect in the interface, not a support ticket.

The measurable outcome

  Before After

Tickets in this cluster16 in 90 days0 in the following six months
Release-strategy escalations from procurementWeeklyNone
Support effort on this clusterRoughly 30 consultant hours per quarterZero

The bigger effect came from applying the same clustering to the rest of the queue. 78% of the open tickets referenced an object, a material, vendor, IDoc, output document or parked FI document, that had already appeared in a closed ticket. The team had not been running a support desk. It had been running a treadmill.

Incident management restores service; problem management removes the cause

Closing an incident and removing its cause are two different jobs, and the case above shows why both are necessary. Maintaining the material group in MM02 was correct incident management: the user was unblocked in an hour. It was also the reason the cluster never shrank. Nobody was wrong. The team was only doing one of the two jobs.

The method, generalised

  • Cluster by object, not by wording. Material number, document number, IDoc number, program name. Wording varies from user to user; the object does not.
  • Ask why three times, in SAP terms. Why the symptom (a blank field). Why the system allowed it (field selection, an interface mapping, a missing check in a user exit). Why it mattered (which downstream configuration depended on it).
  • Separate the trigger from the cause. "A user entered a bad value" is a trigger. "The field accepts a bad value with no check" is the cause.
  • Confirm it in the system. A root cause you can point to in SPRO, SE16, ST22, WE02 or the Data Dictionary is real. A root cause you can only describe in a meeting is a guess.
  • Prioritise by frequency, impact and fix effort. High frequency, high impact, contained fix goes first. The output is a root-cause backlog, not a ticket list.
  • Expect the fix to be config, data or process. In this case one config entry, one mapping change and one MM17 run retired sixteen tickets a quarter. Code was the last resort, and it was not needed.
  • Measure recurrence, not closure. If the cluster stops arriving, it worked. If ticket volume is flat while everyone is busy, the team is managing incidents and not problems.

Where AI helps, and where it does not

The clustering step above took me the better part of two days by hand: 220 tickets, read one by one, mapped to the SAP object each one referenced. That is the kind of work AI can take off an analyst: read the ticket history, group the tickets by the material, document, IDoc or program they point at, and draft a root-cause hypothesis for each group.

Two conditions decide whether that output is worth anything, and they are the same two lessons from the material group case. First, grounding. Each hypothesis has to be checked against the actual system, the configuration, the custom code and the Data Dictionary, so it names a real field selection entry in OMS9 or a real mapping gap rather than a plausible sentence. A hypothesis that cannot be grounded in the system should be treated as unverified, not as fact. Second, a verification gate. An engineer confirms the cause before anyone acts on it, and the AI only reads the system, it never changes it. The MM17 run, the OMS9 change and the interface fix were done by people, through transports, with sign-off.

Used that way, AI does the tedious clustering and the first-pass analysis and leaves the judgement to a person. Used without grounding or a human check, it produces confident root causes that are wrong, and the team fixes the wrong thing faster than before.

The short version

  • A recurring ticket is one unsolved problem wearing many ticket numbers.
  • Cluster by object. In this case, sixteen MM tickets were one blank field.
  • Find the cause in SAP terms: here, an optional field in OMS9 plus an IDoc mapping that never filled it.
  • Fix the condition, not the instance: one config entry, one mapping change, one MM17 run, one owner.
  • Measure recurrence. The cluster went from sixteen a quarter to zero.
  • Let AI do the clustering and first pass, but only grounded in the system and confirmed by an engineer.

Prashanth P M is Project and Delivery Manager at PEOL Technologies, an SAP Partner. The team builds AI platform for SAP operations.

entry.title: Erfolgreiche KI-Adoption im öffentlichen Sektor - Formate, die funktionieren
entry.content:
Beim SAP Discovery Day Public Sector am 10. September in Berlin haben Sebastian Gogolok und ich die Frage zu Beginn gestellt: Experimentiert ihr noch oder transformiert ihr schon? Die meisten Hände gingen beim Experimentieren hoch. Das war erwartbar. Und es ist auch kein Thema, solange man nicht dort stehen bleibt. Wer dauerhaft nur experimentiert, produziert Kosten, Unsicherheit und bekommt eben nicht den eigentlich Mehrwert. In diesem Beitrag fasse ich zusammen, was wir vorgestellt haben: einen Überblick zur KI-Adoption, konkrete Formate entlang der KI-Reise und Empfehlungen, wie Organisationen im öffentlichen Sektor (und darüber hinaus) den Weg von der Idee zum messbaren Mehrwert gestalten können. Auch fragten wir nochmals, was die Teilnehmenden mit KI verbinden. Solche Check-ins geben immer interessante Momentaufnahmen wo Menschen stehen.  

Was KI-Adoption eigentlich bedeutet

KI-Adoption klingt nach Technologieeinführung. In der Praxis ist es vor allem ein Organisationsthema. Es geht darum, priorisierte Geschäftsprobleme in messbaren Prozesswert zu übersetzen, mit dem Fokus auf Menschen, Daten und Governance von Anfang an. Das betrifft den öffentlichen Sektor genauso wie die Industrie, wobei gerade in der Verwaltung zusätzliche Anforderungen an Souveränität, Datenschutz und Compliance hinzukommen. 

Die KI-Reise lässt sich in drei Phasen gliedern: Am Anfang steht die Orientierung mit einem Reifegrad-Assessment, Stakeholder-Mapping und Zielsetzung. Dann folgt die Exploration, in der Use Cases identifiziert, bewertet und priorisiert werden. Und schließlich die Skalierung, bei der es um Roadmap, Governance, ein AI Center of Excellence und den Aufbau eines Use-Case-Funnels geht. Das Muster ist aus der Digitalisierung bekannt. Was bei KI anders ist: Die Einstiegshürde für Mitarbeitende liegt deutlich niedriger, und damit auch das Risiko für Schatten-IT.

Warum Change Management bei KI anders ist

Sebastian hat im Vortrag ein Bild benutzt, das wir auch aus der Business Transformation kennen: die Raupe, die zum Schmetterling wird. Transformation bedeutet, dass sich etwas grundlegend verändert, nicht dass man die Raupe auf ein Skateboard setzt, ihr einen Raketenrucksack schnallt und hofft, dass sie fliegt. Aber genau das passiert oft: Man nimmt einen bestehenden Prozess, der evtl. fehlerhaft ist, und legt KI drauf oder drunter, mit dem Ergebnis dass sie die Fehler schneller produziert.

Die bessere Frage lautet: Warum treten die Fehler auf? Ist der Prozess richtig? Sollte ich ihn verändern, bevor ich KI einsetze? Diese Fragen werden überraschend selten gestellt.

Was KI von früheren technologischen Veränderungen unterscheidet: Wenn ich früher unzufrieden war mit meiner Prozessmodellierung, habe ich mir als Mitarbeitender keine Visio-Lizenz gekauft. Bei KI ist das anders. Wer in der Arbeitsverdichtung steckt und im Arbeitskontext kein KI-Tool bekommt, zieht das Smartphone aus der Tasche und nutzt die private ChatGPT-Lizenz. Mit allen Risiken für Datenschutz und Trainingsmodelle. Das bedeutet: Organisationen sollten sich lieber Gedanken machen, wie sie KI strukturiert ermöglichen, statt sie zu verbieten.

Agenten skalieren: Governance nach Wirkungsradius

Ein Thema, das im öffentlichen Sektor besonders relevant ist, ist die Frage der Agentenautonomie. Einen einzelnen KI-Agenten zu verwalten ist überschaubar. Aber 100 autonome Programme in verschiedenen Abteilungen geraten schnell außer Kontrolle, wenn es keine Struktur und entsprechende Governance gibt. 

Wir haben dafür das Modell "Circle of Control" vorgestellt, das die passende Autonomie eines Agenten an seinen Wirkungsradius knüpft. Im persönlichen Workspace ist breite Autonomie vertretbar, weil das Risiko bei Fehlentscheidungen gering ist. Bei Team-Workflows braucht es moderate Aufsicht. Bei systemübergreifenden Prozessen empfehlen sich explizite Freigaben. Und bei Finanztransaktionen oder Stammdatenänderungen sind enge Kontrollen und Human Checkpoints erforderlich.

 Überblick: Schritte, Rollen, Praktiken und Konzepte der Skalierung

Drei Konzepte helfen bei der Akzeptanz: Agent Champions als Vertrauenspersonen und Multiplikatoren im Unternehmen. Speedboat-Teams, die neue Tools schnell ausprobieren, Feedback geben und als Leuchtturm wirken. Und Agenten Communities, in denen Wissen geteilt, Best Practices erarbeitet und Erfahrungen sichtbar gemacht werden. Frühe und regelmäßige Einbindung verhindert dabei Akzeptanzmüdigkeit. Das gilt im öffentlichen Sektor genauso wie in der Privatwirtschaft.

Ein Möglichkeit der Unterstützung auf der kompletten KI Reise sind die Success Pläne von SAP, wobei mit ganz unterschiedlichen Services die Exploration, Architektur, Validierung, Governance bis zur Aktivierung und Optimierung unterstützt wird. 

Sieben co-kreative Formate entlang der KI-Reise

Den größten Teil unserer Session haben wir konkreten Formaten gewidmet, die Organisationen auf ihrer KI-Reise nutzen können. Alle sind praxiserprobt, die meisten auch branchenunabhängig einsetzbar.  

AI Discovery Workshop

Das Einstiegsformat, um sich zu orientieren. Ziel ist es, in einem interdisziplinären Setting Use Cases zu identifizieren und nach Nutzen, Machbarkeit, Akzeptanz und Datenreife zu priorisieren. Das SAP AppHaus hat dafür ein umfangreiches Toolkit entwickelt mit Workshop-Guides, digitalen Whiteboards und Vorlagen. Der Workshop dauert typischerweise einen Tag, kann aber auch als Kurzformat auf Events stattfinden. Ergebnis ist ein priorisierter Use-Case-Backlog und ein Maßnahmenplan.

Oft ist es das erste Mal, dass IT, Fachbereich und KI-Experten wirklich zusammenkommen und verschiedene Perspektiven auf dasselbe Problem legen. Das ist schon für sich genommen wertvoll, unabhängig von den Use Cases, die dabei herauskommen.

Diese Workshops sind für Kunden gewöhnlich ohne zusätzliche Kosten verfügbar undbieten einen niedrigschwelligen Einstie.g. Quelle: Business AI Explore Workshop

Agent Design Workshop

Wer bereits Use Cases identifiziert hat und einen konkreten KI-Agenten konzipieren will, findet hier das passende Format. Im Agent Design Workshop wird iterativ und gewönlich auf Papier entwickelt u.a. im Agent Design Canvas: Persona des Agenten, Aufgaben, Informationsbedarf, Interaktionsflüsse etc.. Ebenfalls vom SAP AppHaus entwickelt, ebenfalls einen Tag, und ebenfalls mit offenem Toolkit.

Zielgruppe sind eher fortgeschrittene Teams, die wissen, was sie lösen wollen, und jetzt die Frage beantworten müssen: Wie sieht der Agent aus, der das kann? Quelle: SAP ApphHaus Agent Design Workshop Toolkit 

KI-Lernzirkel

Lernzirkel sind kein neues Konzept. Wer studiert hat, kennt das Prinzip der Lerngruppe vor der Klausur. Auf KI übertragen heißt das: Ein Team oder eine Gruppe trifft sich regelmäßig, um gemeinsam KI-Kompetenzen aufzubauen, anhand eines Leitfadens, mit echten Aufgaben, im geschützten Rahmen.

Ich bin ein großer Fan davon, weil ein einzelner Online-Kurs sicher gut Grundlagen und Informationen vermittelt, aber nicht die KI Handlungskompetenz. Die entsteht durch Anwendung, Austausch und gegenseitiges Feedback. Lernzirkel bieten außerdem psychologische Sicherheit und einen Save-Space: Wer unsicher ist im Umgang mit KI, kann Fragen stellen, ohne sich zu exponieren.

Es gibt verschiedene Varianten. In unserer Change Management Community beispielsweise traf sich ein Lernzirkel einmal pro Woche und arbeitet jeweils eine Übung aus dem Leitfaden durch. Natürlich kann man solch eine Lernreise auch etwas steuern und zentral organsieren, oder in mehr kondensierten Workshopreihen durchführen. Teams können das genauso machen. Der Aufwand ist gering, der Effekt auf Vertrauensaufbau und Kompetenzentwicklung spürbar. Quelle: offener KI Leitfaden - Change Management Leitfaden.

Promptathon

Ein Promptathon ist ein Mittelding aus Workshop und Hackathon: wenig Theorie, viel Praxis. Die Zielgruppe sind EndnutzerInnen von KI-Tools. In kleinen Gruppen von drei bis fünf Teilnehmenden arbeiten sie an echten Herausforderungen aus ihrem Arbeitskontext. Gewöhnlich gibt es unterschiedliche sog. Challenges mit verschiedenem Schweregrad. Die Teams suchen sich dann jeweils eine solche Challenge aus. 

Der Input ist minimal, vielleicht zehn Prozent der Zeit. Die restliche Zeit arbeiten die Teams in Breakout Sessions an ihren Aufgaben, testen verschiedene Modelle und Tools mit denen sie auch gewöhnlich arbeiten (können) und dokumentieren ihre Ergebnisse. Coaches betreuen die Gruppen, .z.B. geben Tips oder beantworten Fragen zum HAndling der Tools.

Bei SAP machen wir das intern virtuell mit mehreren hundert Teilnehmenden. Wirkungsvoll ist es auch vor Ort, aber auch virtuell oder hybrid funktioniert es.

Was den Promptathon von einem normalen Training unterscheidet: Die Leute kommen schnell ins Tun. Fragen, Unsicherheiten und Widerstände tauchen direkt auf und können direkt adressiert werden. Das ist Change Management in Echtzeit. Wir haben das auch schon hybrid gemacht, in Walldorf, mit Teilnehmenden vor Ort und online. Die Dynamik, wenn Teams gemeinsam Lösungen entwickeln und am Ende pitchen, ist eine ganz andere als beispielsweise bei einem Frontaltraining. Weiter Infos: Promptathon beim Change Camp + CLC Erfahrungsbericht incl. Checkliste

KI-Communities

Wer Adoption verstetigen will, braucht einen Ort für kontinuierlichen Austausch und Updates. Eine interne KI-Community bietet genau das: einen Raum, in dem sich Mitarbeitende zu KI-Themen austauschen, Erfahrungen teilen und voneinander lernen. Das kann eine Teams-Gruppe sein, ein Slack-Channel oder ein regelmäßiges Community-Event. Wichtig dabei ist due Kuration von Inhalten und die Angebote, sei es Events, Wettbewerbe, neue Inhalte, Umfragen und Ergebnisfeedback etc.

Im Kontext unserer Hackathons (dazu gleich mehr) haben wir z.B. eine Alumni-Community aufgebaut, in der sich Teilnehmende über die Events hinaus vernetzen. Auch intern bei SAP nutzen wir solche Formate intensiv. Community Building ist die Infrastruktur für nachhaltige Adoption. Weitere Infos: Learning & Change Community: LinkedIn - Blogs - SAP Business AI im SAP Community  Netzwerk

Hackathon: Business meets AI

Das intensivste Format ist der Hackathon. Kundenteams treffen sich in einer SAP-Niederlassung, bringen einen vorbereiteten Use Case mit und entwickeln in vier Tagen mit SAP-Coaches ein funktionsfähiges minimum viable Product. Die Coaches sind erfahrene Experten, die täglich mit den neuesten Technologien arbeiten, darunter Joule Studio und die SAP BTP.

Die Applikationen werden auf der Kundeninfrastruktur entwickelt und sind nach den vier Tagen einsatzfähig. Beim letzten Hackathon im März 2026 in Berlin haben die Entwickler selbst gesagt: Was wir hier in drei Tagen geschafft haben, hätte vor einem Jahr Wochen gedauert. Die Entwicklungszyklen beschleunigen sich so schnell, dass wir das Format bereits von fünf auf vier Tage verkürzt haben.

Die nächste Ausgabe findet vom 9. bis 13. November 2026 statt, diesmal als Public Sector and Utilities Edition. Teams können sich mit einem Use Case bewerben. Auch wer nicht zum Hackathon zugelassen wird, bekommt in den meisten Fällen die Möglichkeit, den Use Case mit uns zu besprechen. Es lohnt sich also in jedem Fall, einen Fall einzureichen. Weitere Infos hier im Artikel - Anmeldung direkt hier.

 Micro-Hackathon: 45 Minuten und dann gibt es eine deploybare App

Diese neue Format ist ein Live-Micro-Hackathon nach dem Prinzip Order-Brew-Serve. Teilnehmende reichen eine echte geschäftliche Herausforderung ein, im Besten Fall wird abgestimmt welche Use Cases dann umgesetzt werden. Entwickler bauen in 45 Minuten live eine Applikation, was man auch live ansehen kann. Danach gibt es einen QR-Code, und die fertige App kann mitgenommen werden.

Pilotiert wurde das Format auf der Bosch Connected World 2026. Unterstützt wird der Prozess durch eine eigens entwickelte Submission-Applikation, über die Use Cases eingereicht und qualifiziert werden. An einem Tag können je nach Teamgröße zwischen sechs und vierzig Use Cases durchentwickelt werden.

Das Format eignet sich besonders für größere Veranstaltungen und Kunden mit vielen Geschäftsbereichen. Jeder kann die eingereichten und entwickelten Use Cases sehen und sich inspirieren lassen. Wir planen, dieses Format auf weiteren Messen und Events einzusetzen.

Jetzt anfangen und die KI Reise starten

Der Einstieg muss nicht aufwändig sein. Die Discovery Workshops zum Beispiel sind an einem Tag machbar und meist ohne zusätzliche Kosten. Lernzirkel und Communities lassen sich intern aufsetzen, ohne Beratung von außen. Und beim Promptathon reichen zwei Stunden, echte Aufgaben und eine Handvoll motivierter Kolleginnen und Kollegen.

Was ich aus den vielen Gesprächen mit Kunden mitnehme: Der demographische Wandel wartet nicht - gerade im öffentlichen Bereich ist das ein Thema. Wir sprechen mit Organisationen, die in den nächsten zehn Jahren 30 bis 45 Prozent ihrer Belegschaft verlieren. Das kann nicht allein durch Recruiting kompensiert werden. KI und Automatisierung werden ein Teil der Antwort sein müssen. Und je früher Organisationen Erfahrung sammeln, desto besser sind sie vorbereitet. 

Die Formate, die wir vorgestellt haben, sind bewusst so gestaltet, dass sie den Einstieg erleichtern. Manche sind niedrigschwellig, wie der Discovery Workshop. Andere, wie der Hackathon, setzen mehr voraus. Aber alle haben gemeinsam: Sie bringen Menschen zusammen, schaffen Erfahrungsräume, Experimentierräume und machen KI-Nutzen greifbar.

Wenn du Interesse hast, sprich deine SAP-Ansprechpartnerin oder deinen Ansprechpartner an. Oder bewirb dich direkt für den Hackathon im November. Die Details findest du in den Ressourcen unten.

Welche Formate habt ihr in eurer Organisation schon ausprobiert? Ich freue mich über Erfahrungsberichte und Fragen in den Kommentaren.

entry.title: How the Data and AI Success Plans Help Customers on Their AI Journey
entry.content:
Companies invest in AI units and follow SAP’s Autonomous Enterprise vision. Then the practical questions start: Which agents make sense for us? How do we activate them? And who helps us if our processes span multiple lines of business?  In this interview, Amit Lodhe, Global Service Solution Advisory Leader for SAP Business AI Platform (SAP BTP, BDC & AI), explains how the data and AI success plans address exactly these gaps.

We look into the Data and AI success plans, their cross-LoB entitlement model, and how they support customers at every stage of their AI adoption journey.

What are the Data and AI Success Plans?

Early in 2026, SAP launched the success plan for several areas, also for SAP Business Data Cloud (SAP BDC). Shortly before SAP Sapphire, the AI portfolio was added. Rather than creating a separate success plan for AI, SAP integrated it into the existing plans. The result were the “Advanced Success Plan for data and AI” and the “Max Success Plan for data and AI”.

Each plan has two parts. The data side covers everything in the SAP BDC portfolio: SAP Analytics Cloud, Datasphere, SAP BDC Cockpit, data products, custom data products, and all capabilities tied to the SAP BDC core capacity. The AI side covers all AI use cases across lines of business, from Autonomous Finance to Autonomous Supply Chain.

This integration also follows a commercial logic: AI units as a SKU sit inside the Data and AI solution area. Keeping both under one plan simplifies things for customers who would otherwise need multiple contracts. 

Why Cross-LoB Entitlement Changes the Picture

When SAP launched the Autonomous Enterprise at SAP Sapphire 2026, five domains were released under it: Autonomous Finance, Autonomous Procurement, Autonomous Supply Chain, Autonomous Human Resources, and Autonomous Customer Experience. Each has its own assistants and agents.

A customer buying the Advanced Success Plan for Data and AI gets AI service entitlements across all these domains with a single contract. They do not need separate success plans for SAP Cloud ERP, SAP SuccessFactors, or SAP CX to activate the AI use cases in those areas.

"With the one data & AI success plan, basically the customer is getting AI service entitlements across all the LoBs. We wanted to provide customers a simplified solution. One success plan, that crosses all the LoBs." says Amit Lodhe.

A customer running SAP SuccessFactors, SAP Cloud ERP, and SAP CX can activate agents in all three areas through one success plan. They only need a separate LoB-specific success plan if they have requirements outside of AI, such as for core ERP functionality guidance.

The exception works the other way too: if a customer has only one SAP solution and no cross-functional AI ambitions, the LoB-specific success plan already includes the AI entitlement for that solution.

What the Advanced Success Plan for Data & AI Includes

The Advanced Success Plan works on a flat percentage-based pricing model. Customers get services with no annual consumption limits. These fall into four categories:

  1. Innovation and Adoption Guidance: Product and use case guidance sessions that explain which capabilities are available and help customers understand what is relevant for their situation.
  2. Activation and Optimization: Hands-on work to configure and activate AI capabilities in the customer's own tenant. This is where AI is actually turned on.
  3. Orchestration of the Success Plan: A dedicated success plan expert joins to help the Customer Success Manager to prepare and continuously refine the engagement plan. This person brings specific AI expertise to the planning and execution process.
  4. Enhanced Support SLA: Faster response times compared to the Foundational Success Plan, similar to the former SAP Preferred Success SLAs.

All services are unlimited in consumption. The only constraint: activation services are delivered one at a time (maximum two days of effort per service), sequentially rather than in parallel.

Unified service portfolio one-pager

Why Activation is a Key Differentiator of the Success Plans

"The activation service is one of the most valuable services in the portfolio."  states Amit Lodhe.

The former SAP Preferred Success Standard Edition at comparable pricing did not include this activation. You needed the Expanded Edition (at a higher cost) to get hands-on activation support. The Advanced Success Plan now includes both activation services and a dedicated success expert at the lower price point.

The activation service covers:

  • Joule activation in the customer's tenant
  • Embedded AI activation: features added to SAP solutions over the last two to three years
  • AI agent activation from the Autonomous Enterprise program

Taking Autonomous Finance as an example: three assistants (AR Assistant, AP Assistant, Financial Planning Assistant) with eleven associated agents can be activated through the Advanced Success Plan.

How the Max Success Plan Adds Strategic Depth

The Max Success Plan includes everything available in Advanced Success Plan, adding six further services and a premium service days contract:

  • Dedicated Success Plan Manager - an evolution of the former TQM role, with deep AI and product expertise
  • Premium Support Response SLA
  • Support Case Management Assistant - helps the CSM with ticket management in larger engagements
  • Cross-solution Process Improvement Services
  • Transformation Advisory Services
  • Tailored AI Adoption Services

The last three are delivered through premium service days (a minimum of 36 days, which is part of an extra service contract). They cover architecture point-of-view workshops, Innovation exploration, maturity assessment, tailored AI strategy, Cyber security, Process optimization, Architecture roadmap, Innovation design, Landscape management, Architecture advisory, POC development for custom AI agents, Deployment support and more.

Where Advanced Success Plan helps activate what SAP ships as standard, Max Success Plan helps define the AI strategy, prototype custom solutions, and manage complex cross-solution transformation. More of these advisory services are included in the Max Success Plan depending on customer feedback.

Where do the Success Plans fit in the Customer AI Journey?

The portfolio is designed to be useful at every lifecycle stage:

  • Getting started? The “AI Foundation Orientation” and “Use Case Navigator” help identify relevant AI use cases and define a business AI roadmap.
  • Ready to activate? Activation services turn on Joule, agents, and embedded AI features in the customer’s specific environment.
  • Scaling and transforming? Max Success Plan services support architecture decisions, governance, and custom agent development.
  • Already running AI? “AI Operational Excellence Guidance” shares best practices for operating agents, including ethics and governance.

"In any point in time, no matter what phase they are today, the portfolio is created in such a way that it is helpful for all the customers in all the lifecycle stages." remarks Amit Lodhe.

No customer activates all agents at once. It is a multi-year journey and the plans reflect this reality. That is why services like change management are also included in the success plans.

The Problem the Success Plans Solve

So, what pain points do these new success plans address? The Autonomous Enterprise delivers business-context-specific AI, not generic chatbots. LLMs like ChatGPT or Claude are powerful for general tasks, but they lack the company-specific business context needed for finance, supply chain, or procurement decisions. SAP's assistants and agents are integrated into business processes and trained on the SAP data model.

"The business context is missing from generic AI. Once these assistants and agents are activated, end customers will get very specific answers and outcomes." remarks Amit Lodhe.

Both success plans mainly help customers bridge three practical challenges:

  1. Understanding what is available: Many customers do not know which agents exist or which ones match their processes.
  2. Matching use cases to standard: Before building from scratch, customers need help identifying what SAP already delivers out of the box.
  3. Activating in their environment: Configuration, prerequisites, and change management require guided support.
  4. Extending Standard AI and Build Custom AI: Work side by side from use case discovery, solution design, Proof of Concept and deployment of production grade AI
  5. Optimize and Operate AI: Reliable operations and enterprise-wide scaling of AI with robust governance, security, and lifecycle management

Without this, customers either invest significant time in self-service learning, or default to building custom agents using Joule Studio or third-party platforms, which is often unnecessary when standard solutions already cover the need.

Or as one of the reference customers (SNP) points out: “To get the guidance from SAP experts via the Max Success Plan is the key for our foundation for building the company of the future”.

How the Success Plans Value is Measured

The engagement plan, created jointly by the Customer Success Manager, Success Expert, or Success Plan Manager, defines customer-specific KPIs. These are reviewed in quarterly or half-yearly business reviews.

Typical measurement areas are:

  • Return on investment for AI units purchased
  • Business process efficiency gains from activated agents
  • Number of agents and use cases activated
  • Time-to-value for new capabilities

IDC studies on the Advanced Success Plan and Max Success Plan show general outcomes around faster feature adoption and more proactively resolved cloud issues. As the AI-specific portfolio was just launched in May 2026, dedicated AI outcome studies are still in development.

Practical Tips for getting the most out of the Success Plans

  1. Start with the Use Case Navigator: Before activating anything, use the services to identify which standard agents match your processes.
  2. Think cross-LoB from the start: If multiple SAP solutions are run, the Advanced or Max Success Plan for data and AI is more efficient than buying separate LoB-specific plans for AI.
  3. Plan in quarters, not days: Agent activation is a transformation topic. Build a multi-quarter roadmap with the success expert.
  4. Check what is standard before building custom: Only go custom (with Max  Success Plan or Joule Studio) when standard does not cover needs.

Summary

My takeaway from this conversation: the cross-LoB AI service entitlement is a real innovation for SAP customers. For companies running multiple SAP solutions, this removes a barrier. Instead of navigating multiple contracts and support teams for AI activation across finance, HR, and supply chain, there is now one plan, one success expert, and one roadmap. The fact that activation is now included in the Advanced Success Plan lowers the entry barrier significantly. AI adoption is fundamentally a change management challenge, and guided, continuous support through the entire journey makes a difference.

If you have questions or get more details, then come to our webinar where we are walking the the general Success Plan approach and also look into two real SAP Business AI Platform customer examples: How do Success Plans from SAP help you getting most out of SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP)?  Thursday, October 22 | 1:00–2:00 PM

entry.title: What is the Impact of an Expired SAP On-premise Maintenance Agreement?
entry.content:
SAP still allows access to some information after a maintenance agreement has expired. However, certain services are only available with an active support contract. Login to SAP for Me may still be possible after maintenance has expired, with limited functionality.  

What is still possible: 

  • View existing systems and previously assigned licenses  
  • Access to old support cases (read-only) -Users can still view and access cases even if the maintenance on the installation is no longer valid, (unless the installation number is deleted). 
  • License keys (excluding maintenance certificates) 
  • SSCR keys (Developer & Object) 
  • Access to Security Notes 

What is no longer possible*: 

  • Submitting new support cases to SAP Support 
  • Downloading software, patches, legal changes or updates requiring entitlement 
  • Access to SAP Notes (excluding Security Notes) and Knowledge Base Articles 
  • Accessing full SAP support services such as SAP for Me etc. 

*Please note that after maintenance termination there is a one-year warranty period available for specific support services such as support case submissions and access to SAP Notes.

Who should I contact re expired maintenance? 

You can reach out to your Account Executive as per KBA 2626344 or SAP Order Management (contracts) by e-mailing  sapcontractcenter@sap.com according to KBA 1660069  for help with the expired contracts topics. 

How to find out who my Account Executive is? 

Contact the Customer Interaction Center (CIC) since they can provide this information. There are several ways to contact the Customer Interaction Center (CIC). Be sure to provide the S-user ID, customer number, and customer name, and details of the issue when contacting the CIC team. 

  • Go to the Customer Interaction Center (CIC) page, and choose one from the various avenues to contact the  Customer Interaction Center (CIC): Chat with CIC, Call Us, or by using  Webform 
  • See SAP Note - 560499 Customer Interaction Center: Hotline - Chat - Online Form

entry.title: SNP's Experience with SAP's Max Success Plan
entry.content:
When external perspectives move transformation projects forward

Complex transformation programs regularly reach a point where decisions stall and discussions go in circles. This is exactly what SNP experienced during the modernization of its own SAP landscape. In a conversation, Matthias Schirner, Manager Global IT Business Applications at SNP, explains how the Max Success Plan from SAP helped resolve stalled topics and drive the transformation program forward.

Watch the video interview with Matthias Schirner 

The starting point: ambitious, complex, and blocked in places

With more than 1,700 employees at 34 locations across 22 countries, SNP is one of the leading providers of AI-powered software for SAP transformations and data management. Companies like BMW, Pfizer, and E.ON rely on SNP when implementing complex SAP transformations efficiently and securely.

But even companies with deep transformation expertise face demanding challenges when modernizing their own IT landscape. Four years ago, SNP migrated its SAP system landscape with RISE with SAP to SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition on Microsoft Azure, laying the foundation early for a future-proof cloud strategy. In recent years, this transformation has been consistently driven forward: SAP SuccessFactors for global HR management and SAP Concur for travel and expense management were successfully introduced and rolled out globally. SNP also relies on SAP Business Data Cloud as its central data and analytics platform.

SNP continues to advance the modernization of its SAP landscape. Following the successful move to SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition, the next step in ERP evolution is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

During the program, it became apparent that certain topics were not progressing as planned. Discussions repeated themselves over months without leading to viable decisions.

Learn more about the Max Success Plan

How the Max Success Plan engagement came about

According to Matthias Schirner, the engagement arose directly from the project situation: "It started in a meeting with SAP where we were talking about the status of our transformation program. We came to the conclusion that it would be best to initiate a workshop to talk about specific challenges and clarify how SAP can help us overcome them."

Together, the teams identified the key challenges and prioritized the most important areas for action. From this developed a tailored service engagement specifically designed to address SNP's requirements.

What the Max Success Plan concretely changed

New perspectives on existing challenges

"The main benefit is that we changed the perspective on our challenges," says Matthias Schirner. The external view — combined with SAP's product and architecture expertise — helped reassess stalled situations and develop clear paths forward.

In long-term transformation programs, teams often develop a fixed view of their challenges over months. An external perspective can help identify new approaches and get decisions moving again.

From endless discussions to clear decisions

"Never-ending discussions, a never-ending series of meetings on the same topic — we were able to stop them and convert them into decisions. Clear decisions. And with that, we ensure that we keep moving forward with our implementation."

For SNP, the value lay not only in additional consulting, but above all in restoring the ability to make decisions within the project. That created the foundation to continue the transformation program with confidence.

Fast impact

Schirner highlights how quickly the engagement delivered results: "It was fantastic to see how quickly this service engagement brought value and quality into our project."

Topics that had been discussed for months were moved into solution-oriented implementation together with the SAP experts in a short time.

Why the Max Success Plan is relevant right now

For SNP, the significance of the project extends beyond the current transformation. "We're talking about AI, about Autonomous Enterprise, about agents," says Schirner. "For us, it's important to build the right foundation for all of that."

Many SAP customers find themselves in a similar situation today. The pace of innovation is continuously increasing. Those who modernize their SAP landscape now are simultaneously creating the prerequisites to leverage future innovations such as AI agents and intelligent automation.

This is where the Max Success Plan comes in. As SAP's most comprehensive service offering, it supports companies in strategically managing complex transformation programs. The three-tier model introduced in March 2026 — Foundational, Advanced, and Max — includes dedicated Success Plan Managers, cross-solution process optimization, customer-specific prototype development, and premium support with response times of up to 15 minutes for highest-priority issues. Or as Matthias Schirner puts it:

"Getting guidance from the SAP experts is the key to our foundation for building the company of the future."

What other SAP customers can take away

SNP's experience reflects a pattern familiar to many transformation programs:

  • Complex projects benefit from different perspectives. Even companies with extensive transformation experience can benefit from the product and architecture expertise of the software vendor.
  • Tailored support creates the greatest value. What made the difference was not a standard program, but a service engagement specifically designed around the concrete challenges at hand.
  • Decision-making capability is a key success factor. When discussions produce no results over a longer period, delays affect project progress, motivation, and planning reliability.
  • Future readiness starts today. Those who want to leverage innovations like AI agents or Autonomous Enterprise are already creating the necessary prerequisites during transformation.
 

See below the offical customer story from SNP.

Conclusion

SNP's experience shows that even companies with deep transformation expertise can benefit from close collaboration with SAP. The Max Success Plan helped the company resolve stalled topics, accelerate decisions, and drive the transformation program forward.

entry.title: What's New in Get Support: A Smarter, Faster Support Experience
entry.content:
Getting the right help should be simple, fast, and transparent, and the latest ‘Get Support’ application updates help you do just that. 

Building on a Smarter Support Experience, we're excited to share the most recent improvements to the 'Get Support' application in SAP for Me.

Choosing the Right System

A successful support experience starts with selecting the right system. Making the correct choice helps route your case to the appropriate team and speeds up assistance.

  • Recommended Systems – Get Support now uses the Description you provided to recommend the most relevant systems for your issue. This reduces manual searching, helps you select the right system from the start, and supports faster routing of your case.
  • Search Systems by Product – But if you prefer to choose the System yourself, you can now type in the Product name to filter system search results for faster, more targeted system identification.

Recommended SystemsSearch by Product

Improved Performance & Better Guidance

  • Continued Performance Improvements – Get Support now loads systems faster and keeps case creation moving, thanks to broader performance improvements. Less waiting, fewer spinning wheels, and one less test of your patience.
  • Clearer guidance throughout case creation – Product and product-function recommendations are ordered by relevance accompanied by component information and additional guidance appears before you change the predefined component at the Submit step. The Primary Contact field is also now visually prominent when your case requires it. Together, these updates help you complete cases with greater confidence and fewer corrections.

More Guidance

entry.title: BTP Success Plans from SAP in Action with real Experiences from the Field
entry.content:
We recently ran a webinar on how the Advanced and Max Success Plans work for SAP Business AI Platform (BAIP) and SAP Business Technology (BTP) customers. Together with Amit Lodhe, Global Service Solution Advisory Leader for SAP Business AI Platform, and Dilek Cevikalp, Customer Success Manager for BTP and BAIP, we walked through what these service plans deliver, showed real customer engagements and discussed open questions.  

This post summarizes the key points for anyone who is currently evaluating Success Plans for BTP/ BAIP, thinking about AI adoption on BTP in general, or wondering how the new Success Plan approach compares to what they had before.

The challenges SAP BTP customers face today

Let me start with what we hear regularly from BTP customers. Three themes keep coming up:

  • Slow innovation speed and limited AI adoption. Customers have BTP in place, they see the potential of Business AI, but they struggle to move from "we should do something with AI" to an actual implementation path. And the technology landscape is evolving fast.
  • Increased risk from excessive customization. Many organizations carry a lot of custom logic. When they want to modernize or adopt new capabilities, the complexity of their landscape creates risk. They need expert guidance to make the right architectural decisions, not just documentation.
  • Lack of holistic integration across platforms and applications. BTP connects multiple SAP and non-SAP systems. Getting identity management, connectivity, security, and process orchestration right requires more than self-service content. It requires hands-on expertise at the right moment.

The Advanced and Max Success Plans are designed to address these (and other) challenges. They provide structured guidance, dedicated expertise, and a collaborative engagement model that goes well beyond reactive support.

What the Advanced and Max Success Plans cover for BTP and BAIP

The core idea is that you get a Customer Success Manager (CSM) who orchestrates a tailored Advanced Success plan for you. The CSM acts as your single point of coordination. They build your adoption plan, position the right services, order them, and orchestrate their delivery across quarters. For Max Success Plan this orchestrating role is called "Success Plan Manager", who also can support onsite.

On the expert side, so called Success Experts provide deep subject matter expertise to help you adopt, optimize, and get full value from your SAP cloud solutions. This is not a help desk. It is a structured engagement with regular service planning, adoption checkpoints, and innovation checkpoints throughout the year.

CSM and Success Expert collaboration model with regular checkpoints.

You might ask yourself how the different Success Plan tiers work in practice:

The Advanced Success Plan includes orchestration of the success plan with Success Expert sessions, innovation and adoption guidance, activation and optimization sessions, AI-driven quality and process guidance, and enhanced support SLAs (50% faster initial response on priority 2, 3, and 4 incidents). Compared to the former Preferred Success offering, the Advanced plan delivers more value at the same price point as the former Standard Preferred Success. Customers now get also activation and optimization sessions and Success Expert engagement included, which previously required the more expensive Expanded Edition.

The Max Success Plan adds everything from Advanced plus cross-solution process improvement services, transformation advisory services, tailored AI use case adoption services, the dedicated Success Plan Manager (an evolution of the TQM role), premium support response SLAs, and support case management assistance. 

The Max Success plan is designed for complex landscapes where customers need large-scale, on-site, workshop-type engagements that deliver highly customized results. These premium services are consumed against so called premium service days.

One key differentiator across both tiers is, that the services from the Advanced layer are unlimited. There is no cap on how many services can be delivered per year, as long as they are part of your service plan. To put that into perspective, Amit shared the example of a Japanese customer who consumed more than 120 services in 18 months.

Customer Example 1: From "Where do we start with AI?" to a concrete pilot

The first case study involves a utilities IT services provider. They are an internal shared services organization supporting multiple utilities businesses. They already had RISE with SAP and were actively using BTP. The foundation was in place so to say.

When their internal business units started requesting AI capabilities, the IT team was unsure and hit a wall. They had identified a compelling use case: automating business partner creation from incoming emails. But they had no AI expertise internally and no clear implementation path. Multiple AI use cases from different lines of business were piling up, with no way to evaluate or prioritize them.

Three Advanced Success Plan services were activated:

  • AI Readiness Workshop for SAP Business AI - a full-day session with the complete technical team of eight participants
  • AI Workshop - dedicated follow-up to deepen the practical understanding
  • Expert AI Guidance for BTP Implementation -after connecting the customer's team with an SAP AI expert

The structured engagement replaced uncertainty with clear steps. The AI Core architecture was explained, the pilot use case was defined, and the IT team came out of the workshops equipped to build AI use cases independently. The pilot scope was agreed, and the next phase involves expert engagement directly on the customer's own landscape, moving from learning to building.

This engagement is still in progress. Dilek the CSM continues to orchestrate follow-up services as the customer's AI journey evolves.

Customer Example 2: From architectural uncertainty to a go-live with 4,200 employees

The second case is a large grid operator with approximately 4,200 employees. Their goal was to roll out Work Zone Advanced as their central employee portal.

The challenges were different here but equally blocking. The architectural decision between Work Zone Standard and Work Zone Advanced was unresolved. Identity management was in conflict because Microsoft's and SAP's recommendations contradicted. And the manual effort in content provisioning put scalability at risk.

The Advanced Success Plan services here were the following:

  • Architecture Review for SAP Work Zone: expert validation of the right BTP approach
  • Expert Guidance: a full-day BTP workshop covering Work Zone architecture, Integration Suite, and AI services
  • Strategic Assessment: coordination to resolve the identity management conflict

All of this was orchestrated through Dilek the CSM. Multiple SAP specialists were brought in, each for their specific domain, but the customer had a single point of coordination throughout.

The result was the achieved go-live. All 4,200 employees are now live on Work Zone Advanced. The Standard vs. Advanced decision was made with confidence, without rework or guesswork. Identity management is resolved with clean authentication and security. The foundation is stable and scalable, with manual effort significantly reduced.

What is particularly interesting about this case is what happened next. The customer is now evaluating AI use cases including fraud detection and a payment verification agent. The CSM is already developing the next iteration of the success plan to cover these new priorities. That iterative nature of the engagement is central to how the model works.

The Success Plan service portfolio consists of more than 100 services

Behind the individual customer stories sits a comprehensive service portfolio. Amit walked us through what he called the "super catalogue". This are more than 100 services across all BTP modules.

The portfolio is structured around four promised outcomes:

  1. Continuous long-term engagement with increased productivity. The product expert helps you gain productivity in your execution, as both customer cases demonstrated.
  2. Reimagined processes and accelerated innovation. Through product guidance and innovation adoption guidance, manual and semi-automated processes are replaced.
  3. Adoption of next-generation capabilities and optimized processes with reduced TCO. Activation and optimization sessions involve hands-on configuration work done by SAP directly in your landscape. Trust management, IPS, IAS configuration, connectivity activation, Joule agent activation, AI Core activation — these are configurations that keep the ground ready. A recommendation is to separate core implementation activities (which you can leave for your partner) from non-core activation activities (divert those to the success plan).
  4. Improved operations, performance, and business continuity. Enhanced SLAs provide 50% faster response times during critical phases like go-live.

Portfolio elements across BAIP Technology Foundation (BTP) modules

The services cover platform foundations (BTP administration, security, connectivity), SAP Integration Suite (from foundation to PI/PO migration to custom integrations and governance), application development (SAP Build, ABAP Cloud, Clean Core, DevOps), artificial intelligence (AI Core, Joule, Joule Studio, AI data layer, AI strategy), and automation (process automation, cognitive automation).

For customers with a specific focus on AI, there is a dedicated recommended service plan that covers AI data layer strategy, AI business scenario design, Joule foundations, Joule Studio, and AI Core enablement. And for organizations looking at the broader agentic AI journey, a cross-line-of-business service plan addresses everything from AI orientation and use case navigation to AI trust and compliance, change management, and AI CoE foundation.

Fast Path to Agentic AI

The change management point deserves also some emphasis. When you start introducing AI agents to your workforce and AI agents become an integral part of people's work profiles, that is a significant organizational change. The success plan portfolio includes dedicated organizational change management services delivered by SAP consulting experts. This is not technical change management. It covers the people, process, and governance dimensions that determine whether AI adoption actually sticks.

Customers on the Max Success Plan benefit from services across the full BTP solution lifecycle from Discover through Run covering platform foundation, enterprise integration, application extension, process automation, and artificial intelligence. These services, such as architecture transformation, transformation safeguarding, and business transformation management, are minimum 10 to 15 days in scope and designed for complex, large-scale engagements. Services in this plan are grouped by business scenarios like "Modernize Your Integration Landscape with SAP Integration Suite", "Accelerate Your Business Transformation with a Clean Core", or "Empower Your Business with AI with SAP BTP", which helps customers identify the right entry point.

What does this new Success Plan approach mean for BTP customers?

If you are a BTP customer today, the practical implication is, that you do not need to figure out AI adoption, integration architecture, or platform optimization on your own or in pieces. The success plan model provides structured, expert-led engagement that evolves with your priorities.

The customer examples show the range. One started from zero AI knowledge and ended with a scoped pilot and an enabled team. The other resolved complex architectural decisions and achieved a go-live for 4,200 employees. Both cases share a common thread: a single CSM orchestrating the right experts at the right time, with a service plan that adapts as new questions and priorities emerge. (See the slides below for additional examples). For customers coming from Preferred Success, the transition to the Advanced Success Plan brings more value at the same price point. For organizations with complex landscapes and strategic transformation needs, the Max Success Plan adds the premium services that make a measurable difference.

Next steps

If you want to explore how a Success Plan fits your BTP or AI priorities:

  • Talk to your SAP account team. They can recommend whether the Advanced or Max Success Plan is the right fit, based on your landscape and engagement history.
  • If you already have an engagement (for example, a Preferred Success plan or Premium Engagement contracts), ask about transitioning to the Advanced or Max Success Plan.
  • Reach out to us directly if you are not sure who your SAP contact is - we are happy to help you find the right people.

Questions and Answers from the BAIP Success Plan webinar

Several questions came up during the session. Here are the most relevant ones:

How does the Advanced Success Plan compare to the former Preferred Success? The former Preferred Success had two editions: Standard and Expanded. The Expanded Edition included activation and optimization services and Success Expert engagement, but at a higher price. The Advanced Success Plan now offers those features at the same price as the former Standard Preferred Success. In other words: more value, same investment.

Are there limits on how many services can be consumed? No. As long as services are part of your service plan (created by the CSM and Success Expert), there is no cap. The Japanese customer example with 120+ services in 18 months illustrates the scale that is possible.

Are the activation services different between Advanced and Max? The activation and optimization services are identical. They come primarily from the Advanced tier. Max customers get everything from Advanced plus better SLA and the premium transformation services (cross-solution process improvement, transformation advisory, tailored AI use case adoption). Those premium services are consumed against dedicated premium days.

Can Success Plans be sold through partners? Yes. Success Plans can be sold via the partner channel. In indirect engagements, part of the CSM function is taken over by the partner, who upskills their resources to fulfil that role. There is a clear delineation of responsibilities between SAP and partner, which the account team can provide.

What is covered from the BTP portfolio? Almost all cloudified parts of the BAIP Technology Foundation are covered. This includes Integration Suite, SAP Build, AI Core, Platform Foundation, and related technologies. Third-party products integrated into the BAIP portfolio are not covered.
